issue.title: Fix qr code in small screens
issue.body: ## Description In small screens (like my iPhone 6) qr codes are cut and then can't be scanned. |Before| After| |----|----| ||| This issue shows QR codes complete. The style issue without rounded borders remains, but at least they can be scanned. ## Type of Change - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [X] 🛠️ Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] ❌ Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change) - [ ] 🧹 Code refactor - [ ] ✅ Build configuration change - [ ] 📝 Documentation - [ ] 🗑️ Chore - [ ] 🧪 Tests ## How I Tested This In my iphone 6 - Sign up - Go to settings - Click in share profile button - With other device scan the QR - Check that it works ## Checklist - [x] `just precommit` passes - [x] Related issue linked (`Closes #NNN`) - [ ] `CHANGELOG.md` updated (if user-visible change) - [x] Screenshots added (for UI changes)

My agent flagged this:

> `ios/Runner/AppDelegate.swift:243` installs the iOS keyring store with `wn_install_ios_background_keyring_store_with_access_group(...)`, which is exactly what the app and notification service extension need in order to share the database key through the configured keychain access group. But `initialize_whitenoise` then calls back into `rust/src/ios_keyring.rs:26`, which installs the same store with `None` for the access group. `rust/src/ios_keyring.rs:61` calls `keyring_core::set_default_store(...)`, and that API replaces the existing default store rather than preserving it.
> 
> That means the main app can end up using a no-access-group keychain store after Rust initialization, while the NSE uses the access-group store. The App Group database path is shared, but the encryption key is not, so background notification collection can fail to decrypt/read the same database. Fix this by making `install_ios_keyring_store_if_needed` preserve an already configured default store, or by passing the access group into `initialize_whitenoise` and installing one consistent store from Rust.
>

issue.title: Delete all app data leaves Whitenoise singleton using a closed database pool
issue.body:
## Summary

After using Privacy & security -> Delete App Data, signing in again in the same app process can fail with:

```text
ApiError.whitenoise(message: Database error: SQLx error: attempted to acquire a connection on a closed pool)
```

This appears to happen because the Flutter app deletes all data via the existing Rust `Whitenoise` instance, but the app process keeps the same global Rust singleton alive afterward.

## Evidence

Current app flow:

- `PrivacySecurityScreen` calls `useDeleteAllData()` and passes `deleteAllData` to the destructive confirmation action.
- On success, the screen only resets Flutter auth state and routes home.
- Rust bridge `delete_all_data()` gets the existing `GLOBAL_WN` instance via `wn()?` and calls `whitenoise.delete_all_data()`.
- The app wrapper initializes `GLOBAL_WN` with `OnceCell::get_or_try_init`, so the retained instance cannot be replaced in the same process.
- Upstream `whitenoise.delete_all_data()` calls `shutdown()`, deactivates inbox/relay control, then calls `self.shared.database.close_and_delete_files().await`.
- `close_and_delete_files()` closes the SQLx pool before deleting DB files.
- Subsequent login goes through `login_start`, which uses `self.shared.database`; on the retained instance that database pool is already closed.
- Upstream already has a test comment noting: after `delete_all_data` the database pool is closed, so a fresh `Whitenoise` instance is required for subsequent logins.

## Repro

1. Run the app in the iOS simulator.
2. Sign in or create an account.
3. Go to Privacy & security.
4. Tap Delete App Data and confirm.
5. Without killing/restarting the app process, try to sign in again.

Expected: sign-in works against a freshly initialized empty local store.

Actual: sign-in can fail with `SQLx error: attempted to acquire a connection on a closed pool`.

## Likely fix direction

The app needs an explicit post-delete lifecycle step. Possible approaches:

- Reinitialize Rust after delete by replacing the app wrapper singleton with a fresh `Whitenoise` instance.
- Expose a bridge function that performs delete-all-data and reinitialization atomically from the app config.
- Force a full app-process restart or show a restart-required state after delete, if live reinitialization is not safe yet.

The important invariant is that after full data deletion, no subsequent API call should use the old `Whitenoise` instance whose SQLx pool was closed.

> The member list snapshot at the moment the button is tapped is serialized into the route's `extra` field and then deserialized on the other side:
> 
> ```dart
> final existingMembers = state.extra as List<String>? ?? const [];
> ```
> 
> This works correctly for the happy path, but `state.extra` survives deep linking and process restoration only when it is a serializable type that go_router can handle. For `List<String>` go_router does not re-serialize `extra` when restoring navigation state after the app is killed and resumed. The member list will come back as `null`, and the filter falls back to `const []`, so all current members will appear as candidates. A user who was added before the app was killed could be added again via this screen.
> 
> A safer approach is to fetch members inside `AddGroupMembersScreen` itself (or in a dedicated hook) using the `groupId` that is already in the path parameter, rather than relying on `extra`. The new screen already has `groupId` — it just needs to call `groups_api.groupMembers` on load and apply the filter from live data.

Good catch, fixed in daea87b. The screen now uses `useGroupMembers` with the `groupId` from the route, so the filter works regardless of how the screen is entered. Added a test for the members-fetch failure path too.
